rubric; ENG-4821"
```

Checked before anything is billed, each with its own message: approving a
**native** case (nothing to
approve), a **claimed-exact** one (needs no\napproval), an **unsupported** or **unresolved** one (approval covers a case\nwhose b
ehaviour was approximated, not one whose behaviour is missing), a\n**disabled** or **unselected** one (the run will not execute it
), an unknown\nid, or the same id twice. The flags are refused outright with `--suite`: a\nhosted suite's cases are not the ones t

his invocation authored, so an
authored-id selector has nothing to resolve against.

**The approval belongs to the run, never t
o the case.** You supply an id and a\nreason and nothing else — the approver and the timestamp are derived by the\nserver and froz
en into that run's own snapshot, because a caller-supplied\napprover would file one person's approval under another's name and a\n
caller-supplied timestamp could be backdated past the edit that invalidated the\nclaim. Nothing persists: edit the suite, re-sync,

or launch again, and the flags
are required again.

Scheduled runs and GitHub-App runs cannot approve anything. A scheduled su
ite\ncontaining a selected approximation is refused by platform policy, which is the\nintended behaviour — an unattended job is ex

actly the caller that must not be
able to wave one through.

`--file` pointing at create-API JSON (no `schemaVersion`) is a usa
ge error\nthat names `eval create --file`. The converse is also true: `eval create --file`\non a versioned suite file names `eval
